flags.headline: New 52-week low after CFO discloses persisting vascular/ortho manufacturing constraints
flags.detail: Stryker CFO Preston Wells, speaking at the company-hosted 2026 Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference fireside chat (Sept 8, webcast via investors.stryker.com), said peripheral-vascular manufacturing constraints tied to the company's earlier cyber incident are now expected to persist into Q4 2026 -- a reversal from prior guidance expecting resolution by Q3. He also described a softer joint-replacement environment (hips hit harder than knees, Europe weakest), with recovery slower than management had expected heading into summer. Management maintained its FY2026 organic growth outlook despite both headwinds. Shares fell as much as ~8.8% intraday to a new 52-week low. Wells Fargo cut its price target to $348 from $418 (Overweight maintained) on the news. This is a new operational/execution risk -- not one of SYK's three listed key_risks (forward-multiple compression, profit-margin ceiling, hospital capex sensitivity for Mako) -- worth adding to the next screener refresh.
